title: Billing adjustments and anomaly resolution playbook
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Summary: Define the product and operational requirements for handling billing anomalies (spikes, duplicate metering, retroactive corrections) and for a standardized manual adjustment workflow. Goal is to reduce customer-facing billing disputes, shorten time-to-resolve, and ensure ledger integrity and auditability. Scope: automated anomaly detection thresholds, a triage playbook, safe manual adjustments with approvals, customer communications templates, end-to-end reconciliation acceptance criteria, and telemetry/alerts. Non-goals: full chargeback automation for Dedicated contracts, pricing model changes, or replacing financial/legal approval processes. This ticket drives the PRD and acceptance criteria required for engineering and finance to implement UI/API hooks and for SRE to create reconciliation jobs.
acceptance_criteria: Anomaly detection: system flags billing anomalies when daily token usage deviates > 200% vs 7-day rolling median or when duplicate meter events are detected by identical request_id + timestamp within 60s; flagged incidents appear in the Billing Incident dashboard within 10 minutes.

Triage workflow: flagged incident can be assigned to an ops owner via the Console; triage status transitions (Open -> Investigating -> Actioned -> Resolved) must be tracked with timestamps and user IDs and be accessible via API for audit.

Manual adjustments: finance/ops users with the "billing-adjust" role can submit manual credit/debit adjustments up to $50k with a mandatory reason, linked evidence (PR, logs, or customer request), and one secondary approver; adjustments are recorded as immutable ledger entries with original and adjusted balances displayed.

Safety checks: system prevents adjustments that would create negative historical invoice totals or double-apply existing credits; attempted violations produce a blocking error with a link to remediation guidance.

Customer notifications: when an adjustment affects a customer's invoice > $100, an email template draft is auto-populated and a notification job is queued; outbound notification generation and delivery must be traceable in the incident record.
Reconciliation: nightly reconciliation job reconciles daily meter counts vs ingestion logs and flags mismatches > 0.5% for manual review; reconciliation results retained for 365 days.

Rollbacks and reversals: any manual adjustment must support a reversal action that creates a new ledger entry referencing the original adjustment and capturing a reason; reversals require the same approver role and are tracked in the incident history.

Audit and compliance: all adjustments generate an audit bundle (adjustment metadata, approver, evidence links, pre/post balances) exportable as a CSV/JSON for finance audits; exports must be downloadable by users with the finance role.
SLA: Average time from incident flag to resolution for high-severity billing anomalies (customer-facing invoice impact) must be <= 48 hours for 90% of incidents in the first 90 days after launch.

Testing and regressions: end-to-end tests validate anomaly detection, manual adjustment UI, approver flows, and reconciliation jobs; test coverage must include simulated duplicate meter events and a corruption-resilience scenario where ingestion is replayed.

Observability: new metrics emitted to the billing namespace: anomalies_flagged_total, adjustments_created_total, adjustments_reversed_total, reconciliation_mismatch_rate; these feed into the Billing Ops dashboard and alerting rules configured in #billing-ops.
Docs and runbook: a runbook (Confluence link) and customer-facing FAQ draft exist prior to GA; runbook includes step-by-step incident triage, evidence collection checklist, and rollback guidance.
notes: Decision: keep threshold-driven anomaly detection rather than ML model for initial launch to simplify explainability for finance and customers.
Trade-off: secondary approver requirement balances speed and risk — ops can escalate for rapid fixes, finance retains final authority for larger adjustments.
Integration: requires metering ingestion team to add request_id to events and to support idempotency checks; see GH issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/issues/482.
Privacy: evidence links may include logs; ensure PII redaction guidance is in the runbook and approval screen masks sensitive fields.
Future: roadmap item to explore ML-driven anomaly scoring and auto-propose adjustment amounts based on historical disputes.
